info.bio: The Upsetters es el nombre que se le dió a la banda casera del productor jamaiquino de Reggae Lee "Scratch" Perry. El término proviene del sobrenombre de Lee el cuál era "Upsetter", debido a su canción "I Am The Upsetter", la cuál era una despedida musical a su antiguo jefe Coxsone Dodd, otro influyente productor jamaiquino dentro del Reggae y el Ska.

scenes.name: Reggae roots y dub
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Junto al funk, la otra gran lección rítmica del postpunk: el bajo como protagonista, el espacio y el eco de la producción dub. Las técnicas de estudio de Jamaica (King Tubby, Lee Perry) se convierten en herramienta de vanguardia para PiL, The Slits, The Pop Group y On-U Sound.

mentions.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
mentions.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
mentions.text: …los guetos de Kingston, que prácticamente se habían convertido en un nuevo salvaje oeste; era música poderosa, e incluso músicos tan diestros como The Upsetters no pudieron pasar inadvertidos para un joven Bob Marley, por aquel entonces una de las estrellas de Coxsone Dodd. Pero resentidos por la tacañería de Scratch al repartir las ganancias de una exitosa gira británica, The Upsetters dejaron de lado al genio en 1969 y se unieron a The Wailers, la banda de Marley, aunque finalmente convinieron que Scratch fuera su productor. podcast.title: "World Famous Upsetters" Single (1962)
podcast.body: The band released the single "I'm in Love Again" in December 1962, credited to "the world famous Upsetters," but it featured Little Richard's highly recognizable lead vocal, indicating his covert return to rock and roll recording before his official comeback. "The single was released as by the world famous opsetters but the vocalist on the record was very recognizable."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Little Richard's Backing Band
podcast.body: The Upsetters were Little Richard's trusted backing band, for whom he strongly advocated to be used in the studio, convinced they were superior to session musicians. "He was convinced that his own backing band, the upsets, were at least as good as the studio musicians and he was pushing for specialty to let him use them in the studio."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Studio Recording with Little Richard
podcast.body: After Specialty Records finally allowed Little Richard to use his own band, The Upsetters, in the studio, they recorded the song "Keep a-Knockin'" together in early 1957. "And when they finally let him use the upsets in the studio, he recorded a song which had roots which go much further back than you might imagine."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
